The witness confidence (7/10) sits exactly at the boundary — not strictly "above 7/10" to trigger automatic trust, but far above the "below 4/10" threshold that would trigger fallback to external text. In this middle zone, I weigh the evidence directly. The witness's detailed morphological description aligns point-by-point with the question's pathological description. The external text offers a bare negation with no supporting visual reasoning. The visual evidence in this specific image instance supports the described pathology.

**Yes.** The image shows an opened abdomen with ischemic-appearing intestinal loops bound together by pale neoplastic adhesive bands, consistent with the described presentation of ovarian papillary adenocarcinoma (good but not the best example).
